correctness.rationale: Averaging by the graph action preserves feasibility and does not increase the convex SLEM norm, so the invariant solution gives the global value. For nonnegative directional weights a,b the full product spectrum has nonconstant displacements from 1 ranging between min(a s_n,mb) and a L_n+mb; the formula still holds on the boundary (including repeated eigenvalue 1). A gap gamma therefore requires at least a=gamma/s_n and b=gamma/m. These minima are jointly feasible precisely when gamma meets the spectral constraint gamma(2+L_n/s_n)≤2 and capacity constraint gamma(2/s_n+(m−1)/m)≤1. Either tight constraint forces both weights, proving uniqueness only in the invariant class. The spectral bound is tighter iff L_n+2s_n/m≥4, automatic when n is even; when n is odd this is m≤8 cos²(pi/(2n)), giving the n=3 equality at m=6 and the 7/8 cutoff for odd n≥5. At the Metropolis weights a=b=1/(m+1), the exact gap is min(s_n,m,2(m+1)−L_n−m)/(m+1). For m≥3 the third numerator is ≥m−2 and the first dominates eventually; for m=2 it is 4−L_n, zero on even cycles and the smallest numerator for odd cycles. Taylor expansion gives the stated ratios (m+1)/2 and 6. Replay by the spectrum and inequalities in frozen RESULT.md lines 39–91; verification materials were inspected, not executed.
